posts.text: Introducing the agent-browser dashboard. See exactly what your agent sees. Watch headless browser in real time, manage all sessions in one place, debug with activity, console, network, and storage panels.
posts.notes: agent-browser dashboard: real-time headless browser viewer plus session manager with activity/console/network/storage panels. 93K views, 1662 bookmarks. Major observability story — makes headless agent runs debuggable the same way Chrome DevTools makes pages debuggable. Direct parallel to our own dashboard work.

posts.text: New: Programmatic API for emulate. Automated test suites + local emulators: 1. Create emulator (Vercel, GitHub, Google) 2. Set env var (and/or pass to SDK) 3. Reset data and close when appropriate
posts.notes: Programmatic API for emulate. Allows test suites to spin up/down local Vercel/GitHub/Google emulators per test. Follow-up to the emulate launch — makes it usable in CI pipelines. Low engagement (9K views) because it is a developer-API detail, but architecturally important for agent sandbox workflows.

posts.text: Introducing Generative TUI. Ask anything - get polished dashboards with real data, rendered live in your terminal. 27 components. Streaming. json-render + Ink. npx skills add vercel-labs/json-render --skill ink
posts.notes: Generative TUI launch — json-render + Ink. 27 streaming components. 216K views, 2774 bookmarks. Already ingested as catalogue entry. Direct relevance to our terminal-based orchestrator: means we could render agent status dashboards via json-render + Ink instead of hand-coded tmux layouts.

posts.text: Introducing a new experiment: emulate. Local API emulation for CI and no-network sandboxes with no mocks, fully stateful, full OAuth flows, app registration, production-fidelity API emulation for Vercel, GitHub, and Google APIs.
posts.notes: emulate launch — stateful local API emulation for Vercel/GitHub/Google APIs with OAuth and app registration. Replaces mocks for CI and no-network sandboxes. Already ingested as catalogue entry. Huge unlock for capability-bounded agent sandboxes: agents can do real API-shaped work inside a pure-local emulator.

posts.text:
Auto-discover and connect to your running Chrome with agent-browser

agent-browser --auto-connect open <url>

Or via environment variable:

AGENT_BROWSER_AUTO_CONNECT=1
posts.notes: agent-browser --auto-connect: auto-attach to the user's already-running Chrome instance (CDP). 141K views, 1485 bookmarks. Relevant for agentic workflows where the agent should take over the user's live browser session instead of spawning a new headless one. Reduces friction for 'drive my actual logged-in browser' use cases.

posts.text: json-render now supports YAML as a wire format. JSONL needs a full element before rendering. YAML is valid at every prefix, going from element-level to property-level. YAML looks like source code to LLMs. And we use 3 standards they know: JSON Patch, Merge Patch, Unified diff
posts.notes: YAML-as-wire-format for json-render. Key insight: YAML is parseable at every prefix (unlike JSONL which needs full elements) and 'looks like source code to LLMs', so streaming partial UI is strictly cheaper + more reliable. Uses JSON Patch, Merge Patch, Unified diff for deltas. Already ingested — directly informs how our orchestrator should stream UI updates.

posts.text:
Generative UI for Svelte is here

– JSON specs to native Svelte components
– Runes-based reactivity
– Type-safe component registries
– Streaming UI generation
– State, actions, visibility, validation providers

npx skills add vercel-labs/json-render --skill svelte
posts.notes: Generative UI for Svelte (json-render --skill svelte). JSON specs → native Svelte components with Runes reactivity, type-safe registries, streaming, state/actions/visibility/validation providers. Confirms json-render's framework-agnostic direction.

posts.text:
Introducing Generative UI for MCP Apps

One server. Infinite interfaces.

Instead of building views, define a component catalog. The AI assembles the right UI based on your API, CLI or MCP server tools.

Works in Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor and more
posts.notes: Generative UI for MCP Apps. 'One server, infinite interfaces' — component catalog + MCP tools → AI-assembled UIs across Claude/ChatGPT/VS Code/Cursor. 161K views, 2171 bookmarks. Already ingested. Core thesis overlap with our 70/30 deterministic/LLM architecture. Strongest post of the month.

posts.text:
New agent-browser skill: Electron

You can now control desktop apps built with Electron, including Discord, Figma, Notion, Spotify and VS Code

Or, use it to debug your own Electron app

Add it to any coding agent:

npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-browser --skill electron
posts.notes: agent-browser Electron skill: control Discord, Figma, Notion, Spotify, VS Code via agents. CDP-based. 730K views, 5237 bookmarks. Extends agent browser automation to desktop apps. Major capability expansion.
